001_N: You just picked up a cup.
002_N: Crack. Now there's a handle in your hand. And the cup is on the floor.
003_N: Yesterday you won a fight in a minute. Today you lost to the dishes.
004_HERO: Mom, do we have any metal cups?
005_N: That's the small stuff. One day something alive will land in that hand. Lighter than a cup.
006_N: What if you became Mike Tyson? You'd get his punch, his speed, and his road.
008_N: Your name is Danya, you're fifteen. The strongest thing you've done with your hands is open a jar of pickles. On the third try.
009_N: On your building's roof there's a pigeon loft. Forty birds, and you know each by sight.
011_HERO: They're racing pigeons. They're smarter than you.
012_N: Lyokha is your friend. He has a theory for everything and proof for nothing.
013_N: And then an ordinary morning comes. You reach to turn off the alarm clock.
014_N: And the alarm clock goes into the nightstand. Up to its hands.
016_N: You walk to the door. Take the handle. Crack.
017_N: In the yard, Gera from the third entrance is waiting. Two years he's collected your change. On schedule.
018_N: He swings, just for show. And suddenly you're below his fist. And off to the side.
019_N: Your hand answers on its own. Gera flies onto the bench. Sits up straight, like in an armchair. And gets up offended.
021_N: The whole yard is looking at you. You're looking at your fist. And it clenches.
022_N: Tyson's story began in Brownsville, Brooklyn. By his own account, he kept pigeons as a kid.
023_N: You have pigeons too. Only now it's scary to go near them.
024_LEHA: Right. We need a scientific approach.
025_N: Experiment one. A pencil. You pick it up the way people pick up a pencil.
028_N: Experiment two. You try very hard. Gently. Two fingers.
029_N: The glass holds for a whole second.
031_N: You figured out everything about the egg from the umbrella.
032_LEHA: Conclusion. You've become too strong for things.
033_N: Rule number one: the stronger you are, the more fragile the world around you.
035_HERO: So what now, I shouldn't touch anything?
036_LEHA: Or find someone who touches things the right way.
037_N: In nineteen eighty-four, scientists Westling and Johansson measured how people hold things.
038_N: It turned out we squeeze an object a little harder than needed so it won't slip. Just a little.
039_N: Your margin is now like a hydraulic press.
040_N: A basement gym. It smells of leather and chlorine. The coach is Semyon Ilyich, and he won't shake your hand.
041_COACH: Saw what you did to your door handle. Come in.
042_N: Tyson had a coach, Cus D'Amato. They met when Mike was about thirteen.
043_N: D'Amato taught the peek-a-boo style: hands at your face, body swaying, punches by number.
045_N: You learn the numbers in a day. The slips in two. The body knows it all itself.
046_N: On day three you take a light slap from the mitt. Then another.
047_N: Semyon Ilyich lowers the mitts and looks for a long time. Not at your hands. At your shoulders. They're up by your ears.
048_COACH: Shoulders down. You're not carrying a wardrobe.
049_N: You lower your shoulders. For four seconds. Then they creep back up.
050_N: The coach writes something in a notebook and underlines it twice.
051_N: And then Semyon Ilyich takes out an egg.
052_COACH: Hit it. And stop a centimeter short.
053_N: The first egg. You aim and clench your fist till it creaks.
054_N: The second. The third. The coach silently wipes the ring.
055_COACH: Exhale. Watch the egg, not your hand.
056_N: You exhale. You watch the egg. The fist flies, and stops. A centimeter away.
058_N: Your palm goes down with the egg. Like a hammock. The egg lies in your hand. Whole.
060_COACH: When you figure it out, come back for the belt.
061_N: You didn't figure it out. You decided you were just lucky.
062_N: Your first fight. A community hall, two hundred spectators. Your opponent is older, heavier, and sure you used the wrong door.
063_N: Gong. Slip. Seven, two, three. The referee counts to ten, and you look at the clock. A minute has passed.
064_N: And the next morning you simply pick up a cup.
065_N: Crack. A handle in your hand. The cup on the floor. Yesterday you won a fight in a minute. Today you lost to the dishes.
066_HERO: Mom, do we have any metal cups?
067_MAMA: We do. It's called a saucepan.
068_N: Tyson's first nineteen professional fights ended in knockouts. Twelve in the first round.
069_N: Yours come out the same. Fight, knockout. Home, a phone.
070_N: Fight, knockout. Home, a key stays in the lock. Separate from the head.
071_N: Fight, knockout. Home, a spoon. The third one this week.
072_N: You eat with a plastic fork and carry bags on your elbows. Like a penguin.
073_N: And once, something strange happens. You and Lyokha are arguing on the roof.
074_LEHA: Speaking of penguins. Penguins are fish!
076_N: You argue for four minutes. The whole time you're holding a glass bottle. Whole.
079_LEHA: Note to self: penguins break bottles.
080_N: Before the big fight Semyon Ilyich doesn't come to the gym.
081_N: You're left with the bag, the numbers, and hands nobody tells to "exhale" anymore.
082_N: Tyson had it harder. Cus D'Amato died on the fourth of November, nineteen eighty-five. A year before his student's biggest fight.
083_N: You hang the coach's cap on a nail. Next to the door handle. Very carefully. The nail bends.
084_N: On the twenty-second of November, nineteen eighty-six, Tyson won the title in the second round.
085_N: He was twenty years, four months and twenty-two days old. No heavyweight champion had been younger.
086_N: You're twenty too. Ten thousand in the arena. The second round. Seven, two, three.
087_N: They put the belt on you. Heavy, golden. You squeeze your eyes shut and wait for the crack.
088_N: No crack. You're not holding the belt. It just rests on your shoulder.
089_N: At home, everything is as it was. Mom's glasses.
090_N: The frame with your photo together.
091_N: The tap. The light switch. The TV remote.
093_N: Mom hugs you. You stand with your arms at your sides, fists clenched, counting seconds until she lets go.
094_MAMA: Why are you so stiff, like wood?
096_N: Then, fast. In eighty-seven Tyson held three belts. In eighty-eight he put Michael Spinks down in ninety-one seconds.
097_N: Now you have three belts too, a big house, and people who open doors for you. Literally.
098_N: The handles in the house are steel. The cups are rubber. They still changed the steering wheel twice.
099_N: The railings. The bathroom tap. The lid of a piano nobody plays.
100_N: You moved the pigeon loft to the new roof. You scatter grain from a shovel. From three steps away.
101_N: In a nest at the edge there's a chick. Three weeks old, and the loudest peeper.
102_N: You used to take chicks like this into your palms and warm them. You reach out. Almost touching the down.
103_N: And you pull back. Your hand finds the parapet. The parapet cracks.
104_N: The chick looks at you and peeps. You feed it from the shovel.
105_LEHA: I've got a theory. An egg. On my command.
107_N: You relax with all your strength.
108_N: Turns out you can't relax with all your strength.
109_LEHA: Note to self: on command doesn't work.
110_N: In a week, Tokyo. An opponent almost nobody bets on. Forty-two to one, in your favor.
111_HERO: I'll take him with my left hand.
112_N: The eleventh of February, nineteen ninety, Tokyo. Tyson has thirty-seven wins and no losses.
113_N: In round ten James Douglas knocked him out. The same forty-two to one.
114_N: Your Tokyo looks like this. You step into the ring and don't warm up. Why bother.
115_N: Round one. You swing with everything you've got. And miss.
116_N: Round three. The opponent punches softly. But often. Every time he lands where you stand. You keep standing.
117_N: Round five. You hit even harder. Shoulders like stone, neck like a post. The slips ended three rounds ago.
118_N: Seven, two... The third number doesn't come. Your fist is clenched so hard it can't make it in time.
119_N: Round ten. You see a glove. Then the ceiling. Then the referee, who is now counting for you.
120_N: You get up when it's all over. You grab the rope. The rope snaps.
121_N: The locker room. A plane. Home. You break everything you touch. And for once you don't even notice.
122_N: Night. You're on the roof. Sitting on your own hands so you won't touch anything.
123_LEHA: Where are you? I'm bringing tea. In a saucepan.
124_N: A peep. The chick has climbed out and is walking along the ledge. Below it, five floors and tile.
125_N: Option one. Put a box under it.
126_N: Option two. A net. The handle snaps in half.
127_N: Option three. Touch nothing and wait for Lyokha. Lyokha is on the third floor.
128_N: The chick takes another step. Its foot slips.
129_HERO: Relax. Relax. Come on, relax already!
130_N: It doesn't work. You've been here before. The harder you order your hand, the tighter it clenches.
131_N: And then you remember the bottle.
132_N: You held it four minutes and didn't break it. Because you weren't looking at your hand. You were looking at Lyokha.
133_N: And now everything else. The cup. The handle. The pencil. The key. The glasses. You watch your hand. Knuckles white.
136_LEHA: Uh... Penguins are fish after all!
139_N: You look only at it. Exhale. Your palm goes down with it. Like a hammock.
141_N: It's sitting in your palm. Warm. Angry. Alive.
142_N: You don't remember opening your fingers.
144_N: Lyokha pours tea. Without thinking, you take the cup from him. An ordinary porcelain one.
146_N: Rule number one was wrong. The world didn't become fragile because you became strong.
147_N: Things broke when you clenched. When you were afraid to break them. When you held on to control with both hands.
148_N: In twenty ten, McGill and colleagues recorded the muscles of five strong fighters. Their punches came in two peaks.
149_N: Tense, release, tense. By their conclusion, the arm speeds up between the peaks.
150_N: In Tokyo you didn't lose because you got weaker. You hit with everything, and speed is born where muscles let go.
151_N: In the morning you go down to the basement. Semyon Ilyich is back. You bring him one egg.
152_COACH: No belt. Why did you come?
154_N: He throws. You watch the egg. Exhale. Palm. Whole.
155_N: He opens the notebook. There's one word. Underlined twice.
156_COACH: Well, there. Now we can talk about the belt.
157_N: In the evening you come home. And Mom, as always, goes to hug you.
158_N: You hug her first. With both arms. Nothing cracks.
160_N: The strength stayed with you. All of it. Only the fear left.
161_N: What are you afraid to break?
